Zhytomyr Oldest Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zhytomyrska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Zhytomyr had no substantial Jewish presence until the 18th century, though by 1751 the city already held 346 Jews despite an official ban on Jewish settlement. In 1753, 33 Jews were tried in a blood libel in Zhytomyr, and 13 were executed — one of the most severe documented outcomes of such an accusation in this collection. By the mid-19th century, Zhytomyr held one of only two Jewish printing presses legally permitted anywhere in the Russian Empire, the other being in Vilnius, and the city also hosted a government-sponsored rabbinical seminary from 1848 and Russia's first Jewish vocational school from 1862. This is the oldest of Zhytomyr's three documented Jewish burial sites, closed for burials already in the 19th century and demolished after WWII for construction needs; a block of flats and other buildings now occupy the site.
